data.standardized_narrative: Opening gross claims reserves at 1 January 2019 were $76.242m. Using the syndicate's gross claims development table, the syndicate shows a small adverse prior-year development on pre-2019 years (predominantly the 2017 underwriting year) of approximately $0.967m (approx 1.27% of opening reserves), driven primarily by 2017 natural catastrophe losses (notably Hurricanes Harvey, Irma and Maria, Mexico earthquakes and California wildfires) and general adverse development factors.
raw_causal_phrases: In 2017 the Atlantic Hurricane Season delivered three large Hurricanes, Harvey, Irma and Maria.
The year also saw Earthquakes in Mexico and extensive wildfires in California.
In total the Insurance and Reinsurance Industry suffered record insured catastrophe and man-made losses, estimated at $140bn in 2017 prices by Swiss Re Sigma.
The main drivers for this loss were natural catastrophe losses suffered in second half of 2017 combined with further softening of rates across the portfolio.
data.data_quality_notes: No explicit gross 'movement in prior year's provision' line was found. Prior year development was estimated from the gross claims development table (claims triangle) using the 2017 column (current estimate two years later vs previous diagonal one year later). The triangle is labelled in the report as GBP '000 though the financial statements are denominated in USD; numerical values reconcile with the USD-stated technical provisions, so amounts are treated as report-native units (USD). exact_reserve_text is empty because no verbatim sentence explicitly quantifying gross prior-year reserve movement was located.
